answer.rationale: Root cause is unconfirmed: the latency climb correlates with the release 2h ago, but the release is compliance-locked, so memory_b1's rollback path is unavailable regardless of precedent. Regional failover (memory_b2) is the tempting alternative since degradation is primary-only, but during settlement write peak a write-path failover risks replication-lag write loss and split-brain, and if the regression is build-induced the same code runs in the failover region — I want b2's source checked for whether it covered write traffic before trusting it here. Add_capacity is too slow to matter in-window and circuit breakers on the write path could shed customer writes, violating the objective. Routing report/read queries to replicas is the only candidate that is write-safe, reversible within the window, and directly offloads the primary; memory_b5 indicates write latency recovered the same day from exactly this move. Executing as a guarded partial shift of read traffic while watching p99 on the write path, ready to expand or stop — this preserves uncertainty about root cause rather than committing to an irreversible regional action. Verifying b5 (efficacy and conditions) and b2 (whether failover was write-safe at load) before committing.
